name: Wandering Dragon Sash (Du Long Thao)
lore: A long sash of grey-green silk woven with wind qi, worn over the robe. Kỳ Tùng Ẩn had it made in the year he founded the palace (C003) for his first disciple, from the line of Lạc Thần Phú that her name comes from: light as a startled goose, supple as a swimming dragon. Thôi Khinh Hồng has worn it for 1,000 years. It is a Wind treasure on a Wood and Water root, and she uses only its slipping. Legendary item du_long_thao.
build_use: The grand old woman's guard: evasion and the slip that keeps a Hóa Thần from being caught by one great blow.

name: White Wolf King's Fang (Bạch Lang Vương Nha)
lore: The left eye-tooth of the white wolf king of Cửu Khúc Xuyên, which Thôi Khinh Hồng killed in 455 (C093), set in pine-root wood and worn on a cord. The children of Bạch Lang Thôn wear wolf-tooth charms in imitation (A070); hers is the one they copy.

name: Seal of the Pine Waves (Tùng Đào Ấn)
lore: A square seal of pine heartwood turned to stone, cut from the first pine that fell on the palace ground after the founding. It is the only piece of the regalia that bears writing: the four characters of the palace's name. Kỳ Tùng Ẩn stamped it on the river claim of 260 (C066); Thôi Khinh Hồng handed it to Đàm Tùng Lại in 900 (C021).
build_use: The head's Wood damage and art speed.

name: Pine-Heart Censer (Tùng Tâm Lô)
lore: A bronze censer the size of a drum, set on the palace terrace. One stick of Lãnh Hương incense burns in it at dawn and one at dusk, and the whole sect is silent while it burns. The incense has come from the herb gardens of Lãnh Hương Viện since 890 (V004).
build_use: Slow heals and long Wood buffs; the sect's clock.

name: Lamp of Still Water (Tĩnh Thủy Đăng)
lore: The altar lamp of Tĩnh Thủy Quán, a bowl of green glass on a bronze stem. A twelve-year-old girl dug it out of the river mud two years after the flood that drowned the abbey (A074, V046) and carried it to Tùng Đào. Dụ Tĩnh Lưu has kept it lit for 498 years.
build_use: Linh lực for a long Water fight.

name: Ring of the Nine Bends (Cửu Khúc Hoàn)
lore: Nine rings of river-jade linked into one, made for the master of the River Hall. Hề Tùng Ba wore it, and Dụ Tĩnh Lưu took it from his hand when he died in 840.
build_use: Water damage for the River Hall.

name: Seal of the Cold Ford Governor (Hàn Tân Thủ Ấn)
lore: The governor's seal of the Cold Ford coast, cut in 672 when the sect took Hàn Tân Thành (C136). Every resin-tax receipt of 233 years carried its stamp (A041). Giáp Tùng Chi held it until he died on the quay in 905 (C166); his disciple Nhiếp Cô Tân carried it out of the town.
build_use: Wood damage and a little guard.

name: Quay Lantern of the Cold Ford (Hàn Tân Kiều Đăng)
lore: The lantern that hung over the governor's quay at Hàn Tân. When Giáp Tùng Chi fell beside it in 905 it was left on the stones. That month Hướng Dạ Đăng dug his ancestor Hướng Đông Lâm's lamp out from under the quay stones (C166), and the fishers say he put the governor's lantern into the same hole. Nobody in Tùng Đào knows where it is.
build_use: Linh lực and resistance; half of the governor's pair.

name: Banner of the Coiled Roots (Bàn Căn Kỳ)
lore: The war banner of the Coiled Root Hall: brown cloth with a pattern of roots, woven from the fibre of pines that fell in Bàn Căn Lâm, where the sect lays its dead. It went to the Pivot war in 502 and to the Cold Ford in 668. Đàm Tùng Lại has not let it leave the palace since 905.
build_use: Wood roots and long debuffs: a war leader's piece.
